samples.summary: The stub `gh` answers CI-run and check-run queries without inspecting the SHA, so the new "contract" test cannot detect a regression that unbinds the two unforgeable gates from the PR head SHA (approval/CI laundering).
samples.evidence: mark-ready.mjs's whole security argument is that gates 1 and 2 read separate-actor evidence FOR THE HEAD SHA: `api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs?head_sha=${sha}` (mark-ready.mjs:129) and `api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/${sha}/check-runs` (mark-ready.mjs:151), with sha = pr.headRefOid (mark-ready.mjs:140,158). The stub branches only on `joined.includes("actions/runs")` (test line 57) and `joined.includes("check-runs")` (test line 59) and returns cfg.workflowRuns / cfg.checkRuns for ANY path, and the assertions never look at the logged argv for the fixture SHA "cafe7". Attack chain: an author agent gets a green CI run and an `agent-review-*` success check on commit A, then force-pushes commit B (unreviewed). Today mark-ready re-queries B and the gates fail. If a refactor dropped `?head_sha=`, used the base/merge SHA, or fell back to "latest CI run in the repo", promotion would accept evidence from a commit nobody reviewed — and every test in this file would still pass, because the stub answers identically for every SHA. The file's stated purpose is to make exactly this class of silent regression loud. Suggested fix: have the stub record/branch on the requested path and add a case where the runs/checks are returned for a different SHA (or assert the log contains `head_sha=cafe7` and `commits/cafe7/check-runs`).
searchedFor: read scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs in full (ciPassed / reviewChecks / headRefOid)
read scripts/agent/checks.mjs (checkPassed, allRequiredPassed — no SHA involvement)
grep GH_STUB across the repo for any other stub that asserts request paths

samples.summary: The spawned CLI inherits the full environment (real GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN, real `gh` config); PATH shadowing of an extensionless `gh` is the only thing keeping the suite off the live GitHub API, and nothing asserts the stub was actually used.
samples.evidence: run() spawns with `env: { ...process.env, PATH: `${dir}${path.delimiter}${process.env.PATH}` }` (lines 96-104) and overrides only GH_MUTATION_TOKEN. mark-ready's read path uses `gh(...)` with the inherited env (mark-ready.mjs:79-81), so if PATH resolution ever fails to pick the stub — an extensionless file is not executable on Windows, and any future switch to an absolute `gh` path or a `shell: true` spawn would bypass it — `gh pr view 7` and `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/...` would run against the real repository with whatever token is in the environment (in CI the verify-self job's token, locally the developer's stored hosts.yml credentials). Real mutations happen to be blocked only incidentally, because ghMutate overrides GH_TOKEN with the bogus "stub-app-token" (mark-ready.mjs:93-97) — a defence the test does not intend and does not assert. Several tests would also pass on that fallthrough (the exit-2 "failed to read PR" case passes whenever gh errors for any reason), so the suite can go green while never exercising the stub. Hardening: set GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN to a dummy, point GH_CONFIG_DIR at the temp dir, and assert `calls.length > 0` for every non-usage case so a missed stub fails loudly instead of hitting the network.

samples.summary: The test pins `--allow-no-checks` as a promoting path (zero review evidence) but pins neither its blast radius nor the invariant that the promote workflow never passes it.
samples.evidence: Lines 136-138 assert that `["7","--promote","--require-checks","","--allow-no-checks"]` exits 0 and calls `pr ready` — i.e. the file now certifies a promotion in which gate 2 (independent review approval) is vacuously satisfied with no evidence at all (mark-ready.mjs:70-77 exists precisely because `allRequiredPassed(runs, [])` is fail-open). Nothing pins the limits of that opt-in: there is no case asserting that `--allow-no-checks` still requires gate 1 (CI green) and gate 3 (disclosure), so a regression that made the flag short-circuit the whole `gates.every` check (mark-ready.mjs:180) would promote unreviewed, red-CI PRs and leave this suite green. Relatedly, the file already reads the real agent-review-panel.yml, so it is the natural place to pin the security-relevant invariant that the promote step invokes mark-ready WITHOUT `--allow-no-checks` (today: `mark-ready.mjs "$PR" --promote --require-checks "$REQUIRED"`, agent-review-panel.yml:1392) — a future edit adding that flag to work around an empty `$REQUIRED` would convert the fail-closed guard into a fail-open one with no test objecting.
searchedFor: read mark-ready.mjs:49-77 (REQUIRED_CHECKS derivation and fail-closed guard)

samples.summary: Every run() leaves a world-executable file named `gh` in a temp directory that is never cleaned up.
samples.evidence: run() does `mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), "mark-ready-"))` and `writeFileSync(path.join(dir, "gh"), STUB_GH, { mode: 0o755 })` (lines 92-95) with no removal, so a suite run leaves ~20 directories each containing an executable named `gh`. mkdtempSync creates the directory 0700, so this is not a hijack vector for another local user, but stale executables shadowing a real tool name accumulate in a shared /tmp and would be picked up by anything that later prepends one of those directories to PATH. Cheap fix: rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }) after the spawn, or a single fixture dir under t.after().

verdict.reason: The absence claim is factually accurate — the stub `gh` in mark-ready.test.mjs:57-60 branches only on substring matches ("actions/runs", "check-runs") and no assertion inspects the logged argv for the fixture SHA (the sole `cafe7` occurrence in the whole repo is the fixture at :78; no other test file asserts mark-ready's SHA binding). But it is not a security defect under this lens. The enforced path is intact and SHA-bound: mark-ready.mjs:129 issues `actions/runs?head_sha=${sha}`, :151 issues `commits/${sha}/check-runs`, and both are invoked with `pr.headRefOid` (:140, :158) read at :103-109. The only invocation of the CLI anywhere is the promote job at .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1392, so there is no unguarded alternate call site and no live bypass. The finding's own attack chain concedes this ("Today mark-ready re-queries B and the gates fail") and is premised on a hypothetical future refactor. A test that would not catch a hypothetical regression is a test-adequacy/coverage gap, explicitly excluded from the Security lane, not a missing/weakened authorization gate, secret exposure, injection, or broken cryptographic verification. Legitimate hardening request for the test-adequacy reviewer; not a merge-gate security blocker.
